headline: Learned models generate, denoise, and steer human gut microbiome compositions
label: Learned Microbiome Models
summary: Three May 2026 preprints extend learned models from microbiome description to generation and personalized dietary design.
synthesis: The shared thread is learning models directly over microbial community profiles and using them for generation, inference, or design. Susagi embeds bacterial SSU rRNA sets and uses a permutation-invariant denoising transformer to learn a member-level stability function applied zero-shot. The Second Brain applies a diffusion model with a sparsity-preserving decoder to generate synthetic human gut profiles, evaluated on American Gut Project data. MPDR extends this toward intervention, learning diet-microbe interactions from paired cohort data and optimizing personalized diets toward target compositions. What is new is the attention to compositional structure, including permutation invariance, sparsity, and optimization over controllable inputs. The available summaries do not report quantitative benchmarks, so performance claims remain unverified.
